title: Presenting with Charisma
coreMove: Make an audience feel your attention, authority, and goodwill while carrying them through a prepared point.
sourcePressure: The source identifies presentations as an applied-charisma setting where room-facing delivery still depends on internal state, body language, presence, power, and warmth.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version becomes public-speaking polish. The useful version shows how the presenter makes the room feel held by the message, not entertained by technique.

tryThisNow: Make eye contact with three people

exampleSpecs.domain: a medical device demo in a hospital simulation lab
exampleSpecs.audience: a product educator whose competence can feel like pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether nurses trust a new pump protocol before rollout
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the presenter starts by placing the pump in the nurse's normal workflow, then demonstrates one alarm while watching the audience's hands, not the slide
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an infusion pump clipped to a simulation-bed rail

exampleSpecs.domain: a courthouse historical society lecture on a restored trial transcript
exampleSpecs.audience: a scholar who must turn expertise into felt attention
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether residents care enough to fund the archive project
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she holds up the page with the torn margin, pauses until the room sees the handwriting, then gives the legal context
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a torn transcript page under a document camera

exampleSpecs.domain: a climate adaptation briefing for vineyard owners after a frost season
exampleSpecs.audience: a scientist who needs warmth for people facing loss
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether growers accept a costly canopy change
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he decides to begin with a frost-damaged bud from one owner's row before showing the regional model
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a blackened grape bud sealed in a clear specimen sleeve

exampleSpecs.domain: a ballet company safety briefing on a new sprung floor
exampleSpecs.audience: an operations director speaking to artists who fear injury
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether dancers adopt the transition rules before rehearsal
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she steps onto the floor herself, names the injury worry directly, then gives the rule while facing the dancers rather than the contractor
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a strip of marley tape curling at the edge of a new floor panel

exampleSpecs.domain: a community solar co-op presentation in a church basement
exampleSpecs.audience: a technical organizer whose slides overrun the room
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether neighbors sign letters of intent before the funding window closes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: contrast the data dump with the reset where she turns off the projector, holds up one utility bill, and asks people to find the line she will change
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a folded utility bill beside a projector remote

exampleSpecs.domain: a culinary school knife-safety demonstration for adult career changers
exampleSpecs.audience: an instructor who needs authority without intimidation
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether students follow the first technique safely for the rest of the course
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he predicts they will watch the blade, then asks them to watch his guide hand and shows how the calm pace keeps everyone safer
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a chef's knife resting on a damp folded towel

skillTargets: choose a presentation opening that sends presence, power, and warmth
distinguish charismatic presenting from stage polish
analyze how internal state shapes delivery under audience attention
evaluate whether a demo or object serves the message rather than the performer

tryThisNowSpec: For one prepared point, replace your first explanatory sentence with a concrete object, number, or moment the audience can see before you interpret it.
